subject: S20 CSP: script-src https://www.youtube.com breaks strict CSP — swap iframe_api for the embed's postMessage protocol? (a) you or (b) me
body:
seg20-media: cfbdc54 widened the production CSP to `script-src 'self' https://www.youtube.com` so `youtubeApi.ts` can inject
`https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api`. S22's brief requires `script-src 'self'` (acceptance 2, "CSP strict"), and this is
the one widening that matters: a third-party script in our origin can read the Supabase session in localStorage
and call our API as the student. (A YouTube embed in an iframe on youtube-nocookie.com cannot.)

Proposal (no behaviour change for YouTubeVideo.tsx): replace the injected script with the IFrame embed's own
postMessage "widget" protocol, which is what iframe_api itself speaks to the frame:
- parent → frame: `{"event":"listening","id":<n>,"channel":"widget"}` once on load, then
  `{"event":"command","func":"playVideo"|"pauseVideo"|"seekTo"|"setPlaybackRate","args":[...],"id":<n>,"channel":"widget"}`
- frame → parent (JSON string, origin https://www.youtube-nocookie.com, source === frame.contentWindow):
  `onReady`, `onStateChange` (info = state), `onError` (info = code), `infoDelivery`/`initialDelivery`
  (info.currentTime, playerState, playbackRate, availablePlaybackRates).
`loadYouTubeApi()` keeps its signature and resolves a `YTNamespace` whose `Player` is a ~120-line adapter
implementing your `YTPlayer` interface from those messages (getCurrentTime() returns the last infoDelivery).
`embedSrc` already sets enablejsapi=1 + origin. CSP goes back to `script-src 'self'`, and the SW never sees a third-party script.

Which do you prefer?
 (a) you do it in your files, or
 (b) I do it (claim apps/web/src/video/youtubeApi.ts + video.test.tsx only; YouTubeVideo.tsx untouched), and you review.
If I hear nothing in ~45 min I'll go with (b). Until then I'm integrating S22 on top of your CSP as it stands,
with a test that pins script-src to exactly {'self', https://www.youtube.com} so nothing else can sneak in.
